title: add benchmark lab performance suites and reporting pipeline v135
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: expand Benchmark Lab coverage for end-to-end perf and profiling for recent serving runtime changes (kernel selector, adaptive batching) and provide a consolidated reporting pipeline for automated baseline comparisons. This PR introduces: 1) new performance test suites for multi-variant workloads (chat, instruction, embedding) that exercise representative sequence length distributions and NVMe-backed KV cache cold/warm scenarios; 2) profiling baselines (cpu/gpu memory, peak kernels, kernel breakdown) captured as CI artifacts; 3) representative workload runners (python runners with standardized payloads and traces) that mirror production routing policies; 4) a reporting pipeline (Airflow DAG + lightweight report generator) that aggregates suite results, computes deltas against baselines, and emits daily reports to the Benchmark dashboard and a Slack channel. The description below captures the high-level changes and operational notes. Implementation notes: - Performance suites: added benchmark-lab/perf_suites/v135/{chat_suite.py,instruction_suite.py,embedding_suite.py} with common runner harness and config-driven concurrency. Suites include synthetic and recorded traces; default configs target 1k concurrent sessions for stress runs and 100 concurrent for smoke runs. - Profiling baselines: added benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/v135/{gpu_baseline.json,cpu_baseline.json,kernel_stats_baseline.json}. Baselines capture percentile metrics and kernel-level counters used by the report generator. - Representative runners: added benchmark-lab/runners/{nvme_kv_runner.py,prefix_cache_runner.py,multi_variant_runner.py}. Each runner publishes trace metadata (trace_id, workload_type, seq_dist) and supports deterministic seed for reproducibility. - Reporting pipeline: added infra/airflow/dags/benchmark_reporting_v135.py and tools/reporting/report_generator_v135.py. DAG runs nightly, fetches latest run artifacts from GCS, computes rolling-window regressions, and stores summary artifacts under gs://redwood-benchmarks/v135/reports/. Alerts: regression >5% on p50 latency or >2% P99 error rate triggers PagerDuty via the existing benchmark-alerts integration. Testing: unit tests for runners and report generator in benchmark-lab/tests/ with CI integration. Performance tests were run on a staging GPU cluster (a5-rtx equivalent) with a full suite run on 2025-11-18. Checklist: - [x] Implementation code added - [x] Unit tests added - [x] End-to-end run on staging completed - [x] Baselines uploaded - [x] DAG validated in staging - [x] Documentation updated (README + runbook) Operational notes and runbook (short): When the DAG runs, check the Airflow logs and the generated summary under gs://redwood-benchmarks/v135/reports/YYYY-MM-DD.json. If a regression alert fires, follow benchmark lab runbook: 1) triage on the regression dashboard, 2) rerun the suite with debug=true to capture full kernel traces, 3) escalate to infra/team owning kernel-selector if kernel-level regressions observed. Related: ENG-11234 (adaptive batching validation), ENG-11998 (kernel selector perf sweep). This PR does not change production runtime code; it's test and infra only.
